And (does) not feel the urge to feed the poor

item.title: Al-Maa'un:4
item.description:
Al-Maa'un:4 - فَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُصَلِّينَ
fawaylun lil'muṣallīna
So woe to those who pray

item.title: Al-Maa'un:5
item.description:
Al-Maa'un:5 - اَلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ
alladhīna hum ʿan ṣalātihim sāhūna
Those who they about their prayers (are) neglectful

item.title: Al-Maa'un:6
item.description:
Al-Maa'un:6 - اَلَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ
alladhīna hum yurāūna
Those who they make show

item.title: Al-Maa'un:7
item.description:
Al-Maa'un:7 - وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ
wayamnaʿūna l-māʿūna
And they deny [the] small kindnesses

item.title: 108. الكوثر (Al-Kawthar)
item.description:
The surah that informs the Prophet Muḥammad that God has gifted him with Abundance goodness in this life and far greater resplendence in the Hereafter—for which he is instructed to ever show gratitude and charitable generosity. It takes its name from "the abundance" (al-kawthar) mentioned in verse 1. The surah comes to reassure the Prophet Muḥammad and as a retort to his enemy.
The surah is also known as: Abundant Goodness, Plenty, Pre-eminence, The Great Abundance.

108:1
إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ
innā aʿṭaynāka l-kawthara
Indeed, We We have given you Al-Kauthar

108:2
فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ
faṣalli lirabbika wa-in'ḥar
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice

108:3
إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْأَبْتَرُ
inna shāni-aka huwa l-abtaru
Indeed your enemy he (is) the one cut off

item.title: Al-Kawthar:1
item.description:
Al-Kawthar:1 - إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ
innā aʿṭaynāka l-kawthara
Indeed, We We have given you Al-Kauthar

item.title: Al-Kawthar:2
item.description:
Al-Kawthar:2 - فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ faṣalli lirabbika wa-in'ḥar So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
  • [1] Or 'raise your hands.' According to this interpretation, the phrase refers to the raising of the hands to the ears during prayers.

item.title: Al-Kawthar:3
item.description:
Al-Kawthar:3 - إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْأَبْتَرُ
inna shāni-aka huwa l-abtaru
Indeed your enemy he (is) the one cut off

item.title: 109. الكافرون (Al-Kaafiroon)
item.description:
The surah that instructs the Prophet Muḥammad to inform The Faithless that the worship of false deities and the worship of One God are not, and can never be, compatible. It takes its name from "the faithless" (al-kāfirūn) mentioned in verse 1. The surah tells about some of the idolaters that suggested to the Prophet as a compromise that he should worship their gods for a year and they should worship his for a year. This was the reply.
The surah is also known as: The Disbelievers, The Rejecters, The Unbelievers, Those who reject Faith.

109:1
قُلْ يَاأَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ
qul yāayyuhā l-kāfirūna
Say O disbelievers

109:2
لَا أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
lā aʿbudu mā taʿbudūna
Not I worship what you worship

109:3
وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ
walā antum ʿābidūna mā aʿbudu
And not you (are) worshippers (of) what I worship

item.title: Al-Kaafiroon:1
item.description:
Al-Kaafiroon:1 - قُلْ يَاأَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ
qul yāayyuhā l-kāfirūna
Say O disbelievers

item.title: Al-Kaafiroon:2
item.description:
Al-Kaafiroon:2 - لَا أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
lā aʿbudu mā taʿbudūna
Not I worship what you worship

item.title: Al-Kaafiroon:3
item.description:
Al-Kaafiroon:3 - وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ
walā antum ʿābidūna mā aʿbudu
And not you (are) worshippers (of) what I worship

item.title: Al-Kaafiroon:4
item.description:
Al-Kaafiroon:4 - وَلَا أَنَا عَابِدٌ مَا عَبَدْتُمْ
walā anā ʿābidun mā ʿabadttum
And not I am a worshipper (of) what you worship

item.title: Al-Kaafiroon:5
item.description:
Al-Kaafiroon:5 - وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ
walā antum ʿābidūna mā aʿbudu
And not you (are) worshippers (of) what I worship

item.title: Al-Kaafiroon:6
item.description:
Al-Kaafiroon:6 - لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ
lakum dīnukum waliya dīni
For you (is) your religion and for me (is) my religion

item.title: 110. النصر (An-Nasr)
item.description:
The surah that informs the Prophet Muḥammad that The Help of God is imminent in the liberation of Mecca from idolatry, in the throngs whose hearts God will open to Islam, and in the approach of his own passing to the mercy of God. It takes its name from verse 1, in which the phrase "naṣr Allah" (meaning "Allah's help") occurs.
The surah is also known as: (Divine) Support, The Ultimate Victory.

110:1
إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ
idhā jāa naṣru l-lahi wal-fatḥu
When comes (the) Help (of) Allah and the Victory

110:2
وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا
wara-ayta l-nāsa yadkhulūna fī dīni l-lahi afwājan
And you see the people entering into (the) religion (of) Allah (in) multitudes

110:3
فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّابًا
fasabbiḥ biḥamdi rabbika wa-is'taghfir'hu innahu kāna tawwāban
Then glorify with (the) praises (of) your Lord and ask His forgiveness Indeed, He is Oft-Returning

item.title: An-Nasr:1
item.description:
An-Nasr:1 - إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ
idhā jāa naṣru l-lahi wal-fatḥu
When comes (the) Help (of) Allah and the Victory

item.title: An-Nasr:2
item.description:
An-Nasr:2 - وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا
wara-ayta l-nāsa yadkhulūna fī dīni l-lahi afwājan
And you see the people entering into (the) religion (of) Allah (in) multitudes

item.title: An-Nasr:3
item.description:
An-Nasr:3 - فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّابًا
fasabbiḥ biḥamdi rabbika wa-is'taghfir'hu innahu kāna tawwāban
Then glorify with (the) praises (of) your Lord and ask His forgiveness Indeed, He is Oft-Returning

item.title: 111. المسد (Al-Masad)
item.description:
The surah that mentions the Palm Fibre rope that in Hellfire shall be twisted around the neck of the wife of the Prophet's uncle, who bitterly opposed Islam; for she took great pride in wearing an ostentatious necklace she became known for and would slip by night to strew thorns and prickly plants in the Prophet's path to injure his feet. It takes its name from verse 5 in which the phrase "ḥablun min masad" (meaning "a rope of palm fibre") occurs.
The surah is also known as: Abu Lahab, Fibre, Perish, The Flame, The Palm-Fibre Rope.

111:1
تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
tabbat yadā abī lahabin watabba
Perish (the) hands (of) Abu Lahab and perish he

111:2
مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ
mā aghnā ʿanhu māluhu wamā kasaba
Not (will) avail him his wealth and what he earned

111:3
سَيَصْلَى نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ
sayaṣlā nāran dhāta lahabin
He will be burnt (in) a Fire of Blazing Flames

item.title: Al-Masad:1
item.description:
Al-Masad:1 - تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
tabbat yadā abī lahabin watabba
Perish (the) hands (of) Abu Lahab and perish he

item.title: Al-Masad:2
item.description:
Al-Masad:2 - مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ
mā aghnā ʿanhu māluhu wamā kasaba
Not (will) avail him his wealth and what he earned

item.title: Al-Masad:3
item.description:
Al-Masad:3 - سَيَصْلَى نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ
sayaṣlā nāran dhāta lahabin
He will be burnt (in) a Fire of Blazing Flames

item.title: Al-Masad:4
item.description:
Al-Masad:4 - وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ wa-im'ra-atuhu ḥammālata l-ḥaṭabi And his wife (the) carrier (of) firewood
  • [1] Or 'the informer.'

item.title: Al-Masad:5
item.description:
Al-Masad:5 - فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ
fī jīdihā ḥablun min masadin
In her neck (will be) a rope of palm-fiber

item.title: 112. الإخلاص (Al-Ikhlaas)
item.description:
The surah whose six elements of belief constitute pure sincerity of faith or Monotheism, wherein a believer affirms God's divinity, Oneness, and eternality, and negates in relation to Him any offspring, ancestry, or likeness. It negates any kind of anthropomorphism that may compromise pure monotheism. It is unusual in having as its title a term not mentioned in the body of the surah. The word "Ikhlas" conveys the meaning of sincerity in one's religion and total dedication to the One true God.
The surah is also known as: Divine Unity, Oneness, Pure Faith, Pure Sincerity, Pure Truth, Purity (of Faith), Sincere Religion, Sincerity, The Purity of Faith, Unity.

112:1
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
qul huwa l-lahu aḥadun
Say He (is) Allah the One

112:2
اَللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
al-lahu l-ṣamadu
Allah the Eternal, the Absolute

112:3
لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
lam yalid walam yūlad
Not He begets and not He is begotten

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:1
item.description:
Al-Ikhlaas:1 - قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
qul huwa l-lahu aḥadun
Say He (is) Allah the One

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:2
item.description:
Al-Ikhlaas:2 - اَللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
al-lahu l-ṣamadu
Allah the Eternal, the Absolute

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:3
item.description:
Al-Ikhlaas:3 - لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
lam yalid walam yūlad
Not He begets and not He is begotten

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:4
item.description:
Al-Ikhlaas:4 - وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
walam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥadun
And not is for Him equivalent any [one]

item.title: 113. الفلق (Al-Falaq)
item.description:
The surah that opens with the mention of God as the Lord of The Daybreak and that teaches one to seek refuge in Him from the evil in creation and from all who envy the blessings of God in others. It takes its name from "the daybreak" (al-falaq) mentioned in verse 1. The surah is used as an invocation against evil.
The surah is also known as: The Dawn, The Rising Day.

113:1
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ
qul aʿūdhu birabbi l-falaqi
Say I seek refuge in (the) Lord (of) the dawn

113:2
مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
min sharri mā khalaqa
From (the) evil (of) what He created

113:3
وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
wamin sharri ghāsiqin idhā waqaba
And from (the) evil (of) darkness when it spreads

item.title: Al-Falaq:1
item.description:
Al-Falaq:1 - قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ
qul aʿūdhu birabbi l-falaqi
Say I seek refuge in (the) Lord (of) the dawn

item.title: Al-Falaq:2
item.description:
Al-Falaq:2 - مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
min sharri mā khalaqa
From (the) evil (of) what He created

item.title: Al-Falaq:3
item.description:
Al-Falaq:3 - وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
wamin sharri ghāsiqin idhā waqaba
And from (the) evil (of) darkness when it spreads

item.title: Al-Falaq:4
item.description:
Al-Falaq:4 - وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ
wamin sharri l-nafāthāti fī l-ʿuqadi
And from (the) evil (of) the blowers in the knots

item.title: Al-Falaq:5
item.description:
Al-Falaq:5 - وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
wamin sharri ḥāsidin idhā ḥasada
And from (the) evil (of) an envier when he envies

item.title: 114. الناس (An-Naas)
item.description:
The surah that opens with the mention of God as the Lord of Humans and teaches one to seek refuge in Him from the whisperings of Satan and those of evil jinn and people. It takes its name from the word "people" or "mankind" (al-nās) which recurs throughout the surah. This is another surah commonly used as an invocation against evil.
The surah is also known as All People, Humankind, Mankind, People, The Men

114:1
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ
qul aʿūdhu birabbi l-nāsi
Say I seek refuge in (the) Lord (of) mankind

114:2
مَلِكِ النَّاسِ
maliki l-nāsi
(The) King (of) mankind

114:3
إِلَهِ النَّاسِ
ilāhi l-nāsi
(The) God (of) mankind

item.title: An-Naas:1
item.description:
An-Naas:1 - قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ
qul aʿūdhu birabbi l-nāsi
Say I seek refuge in (the) Lord (of) mankind

item.title: An-Naas:2
item.description:
An-Naas:2 - مَلِكِ النَّاسِ
maliki l-nāsi
(The) King (of) mankind

item.title: An-Naas:3
item.description:
An-Naas:3 - إِلَهِ النَّاسِ
ilāhi l-nāsi
(The) God (of) mankind

item.title: An-Naas:4
item.description:
An-Naas:4 - مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ
min sharri l-waswāsi l-khanāsi
From (the) evil (of) the whisperer the one who withdraws

item.title: An-Naas:5
item.description:
An-Naas:5 - اَلَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ
alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūri l-nāsi
The one who whispers in (the) breasts (of) mankind

item.title: An-Naas:6
item.description:
An-Naas:6 - مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
mina l-jinati wal-nāsi
From the jinn and men
